features.name: Agentic systems design
features.description: Experience designing agent-based systems, especially bounded autonomy, orchestration, guardrails, permissions, or auditability.

levels.descriptor: No direct agentic-system design described.
Mentions agents, automation, or multi-step workflows only in broad terms.
Clear experience pairing agents with back-end services or constraints.
Sophisticated description of agent autonomy plus guardrails such as permissions, auditing, bounded actions, or explicit control planes.

features.name: Algorithmic fluency
features.description: Practical command of data structures and algorithms shown through concrete engineering examples.

levels.descriptor: No algorithmic strength is mentioned.
Algorithmic fluency is claimed, but without a concrete example.
At least one specific redesign or optimization shows applied algorithmic thinking.
Multiple or especially vivid examples show data structures and algorithms materially shaping system design.

features.name: Applied AI production maturity
features.description: Hands-on experience shipping AI or LLM-backed systems in production with attention to reliability, evaluation, and failure modes.

levels.descriptor: No AI evidence.
Only vague, aspirational, or lightly specified AI mention.
Shows concrete experience shipping AI or LLM-backed functionality.
Shows concrete production AI work plus explicit evaluation, guardrails, correctness, or failure-mode management.

features.name: Collaborative learning posture
features.description: Openness to learning from and partnering with security specialists or internal users rather than presenting the work as purely solo expertise.

levels.descriptor: Does not signal collaboration with security specialists or users of the tooling.
Uses general teamwork or internal-customer language, but without much specificity.
Explicitly wants to work closely with security engineers, learn from domain specialists, or build in tight proximity to the teams served.

features.name: Developer enablement mindset
features.description: Whether the letter frames security tooling as helping developers take the safe path with less friction rather than policing them.

levels.descriptor: Does not discuss the needs or behavior of developer users.
Mentions helping teams in generic terms.
Explicitly focuses on reducing friction or making the secure path easier for developers.
Shows clear empathy for busy engineers and explains adoption in terms of defaults, workflows, and usable tooling rather than process.

features.name: Engineering rigor
features.description: Whether the applicant emphasizes correctness, reliability, maintenance, testing, and careful boundaries appropriate to security-sensitive systems.

levels.descriptor: The letter gives little signal about quality, testing, reliability, or maintainability.
The letter gestures at seriousness or standards, but without concrete habits or practices.
The letter clearly emphasizes dependable systems, testing, maintainability, guardrails, or careful design.
The letter strongly signals security-critical rigor, with explicit habits such as typed or tested tooling, auditable boundaries, reliability-first design, or builder-quality standards.

features.name: Evidence specificity
features.description: How much the letter backs claims with concrete mechanisms, examples, scope, or named artifacts rather than generic assertions.

levels.descriptor: Relies mostly on broad claims with little supporting detail.
Names some relevant work but gives limited mechanism or outcome detail.
Provides clear examples of work with enough detail to judge fit.
Provides multiple specific examples tied to mechanisms, tradeoffs, or outcomes.

features.name: Formal education
features.description: Level of formal academic training in computer science or a related technical field presented in the letter.

levels.descriptor: No relevant degree or equivalent preparation is mentioned.
Mentions a bachelor's degree or equivalent.
Mentions a master's degree.
Mentions a doctoral degree.

features.name: Go depth
features.description: How central and production-grade Go appears in the applicant's backend engineering experience.

levels.descriptor: No meaningful Go evidence.
Mentions Go, but without clear depth or ownership.
Shows regular production use of Go in recent work.
Makes Go clearly central, such as a principal language or daily driver tied to sustained backend ownership.

features.name: Impact articulation
features.description: How clearly the letter states the outcomes or operational effects of the applicant's work.

levels.descriptor: Lists responsibilities or technologies without explaining what changed because of the work.
Suggests benefit, but the outcome remains vague or implied.
Gives a clear before-and-after or operational result, such as a queue becoming routed, a bottleneck disappearing, or hours being saved.
Shows strong leverage-oriented impact articulation, tying the work to measurable capacity, broad downstream benefit, or a transformed operating model.

features.name: Language breadth
features.description: Range of programming languages the applicant cites beyond the core stack.

levels.descriptor: No additional languages are mentioned.
Mentions 1 to 2 additional languages.
Mentions 3 to 5 additional languages.
Mentions more than 5 additional languages.

features.name: Mechanical polish
features.description: Surface correctness and professionalism of the writing, including spelling, grammar, and proofreading.

levels.descriptor: Frequent errors distract from the content or make the letter feel careless.
Several noticeable errors appear, though the meaning remains clear.
Only a few minor slips appear and they do not materially hurt readability.
Virtually error-free copy that reads as fully polished.

features.name: Narrative cohesion and voice
features.description: How coherent, distinctive, and smoothly structured the letter's overall story and prose feel.

levels.descriptor: The letter reads like disconnected bullets, fragments, or stacked claims.
The letter has some structure, but transitions or the overall arc are uneven.
The letter coherently links background, technical experience, and interest in the role.
The letter presents an especially well-shaped narrative that makes the applicant's trajectory and fit feel natural.

features.name: Offensive security practice
features.description: Evidence of ongoing attacker-minded or offensive-security practice outside ordinary product work, especially through CTFs.

levels.descriptor: No offensive-security practice is mentioned.
Shows occasional or casual participation in CTFs or similar practice.
Shows sustained participation in CTFs or other regular adversarial practice.
Shows sustained adversarial practice with strong competitive results or clearly serious investment.

features.name: Open-source stewardship
features.description: Degree of contribution, upstream responsibility, or maintenance ownership in public/open-source software used beyond the applicant's immediate team.

levels.descriptor: No open-source contribution or maintenance described.
Mentions occasional upstream patches or light contribution.
Shows active contribution or maintenance with review or release responsibility.
Maintains a used project or framework with sustained community, release, review, or user-support responsibilities.

features.name: Ownership level
features.description: How directly the letter shows the applicant personally led, owned, and delivered the cited work or systems.

levels.descriptor: The letter reads mostly as passive, resume-like claims with little direct ownership.
The letter shows some first-person ownership, but mainly on isolated tasks or narrow pieces of work.
The letter uses clear builder language around multiple shipped systems, automations, or redesigns.
The letter repeatedly shows end-to-end ownership, architecture, delivery, and ongoing operational responsibility.

features.name: Personal project ambition
features.description: Technical ambition, scope, and seriousness of self-directed projects outside the day job.

levels.descriptor: No side project is mentioned, or the example is very small and shows little technical challenge.
A modest personal project is described, showing completion but limited system complexity.
A substantial project is described, involving meaningful systems design, edge cases, or failure handling.
An especially ambitious project is described, such as a distributed or production-like system built to explore hard engineering problems deeply.

features.name: Platform leverage orientation
features.description: Motivation toward foundational or shared infrastructure work whose benefits compound across many teams or systems.

levels.descriptor: No platform-level or organization-wide leverage framing is present.
The letter expresses generic interest in scale or broad impact.
The letter explicitly frames motivation around foundational infrastructure, inherited improvements, or organization-wide leverage.

features.name: Production experience depth
features.description: Overall maturity of production software experience when the dimension combines tenure, shipped systems, and ownership into one signal.

levels.descriptor: Only minimal relevant experience is conveyed, with short tenure, narrow scope, or ambiguous ownership.
Clear early-career production experience is shown, but the record is still limited in depth or breadth.
Solid production background is shown through several years of work with repeated launch and maintenance responsibility.
Extensive directly relevant background is shown through long tenure plus broad multi-service responsibility.

features.name: Production ownership breadth
features.description: Breadth of concrete production-service launch, maintenance, and operational ownership described in the letter.

levels.descriptor: No clear production delivery record, or only one service mentioned.
A modest production record, typically 2 services.
A solid production record, typically 3 to 4 services.
A broad production record, typically 5 or more services with clear launch or ownership experience.

features.name: Python depth
features.description: How substantial and production-grade the applicant's Python experience appears for services, tooling, automation, or agents.

levels.descriptor: No Python evidence, or Python is only named without context.
Python is mentioned for basic scripting or generic use.
Shows substantial production Python use in services, automation, or internal tooling.
Shows deep production Python use with quality signals such as typed, tested, extensible, or central security tooling.

features.name: Relevant tenure
features.description: Amount of directly relevant post-school professional software-engineering experience the applicant claims.

levels.descriptor: Below the role minimum or unclear on relevant experience length.
Roughly meets the minimum, around 2 to 3 years of relevant experience.
Shows solid mid-level experience, around 4 to 5 years.
Shows strong experience depth, around 6 or more years.

features.name: Role-specific fit
features.description: How specifically the letter explains why this exact role is a compelling and coherent fit for the applicant.

levels.descriptor: Shows generic interest in applying with little reason for this role in particular.
States interest in the role but with broad or familiar reasoning.
Gives a clear role-specific reason tied to security engineering, automation, or impact.
Articulates a distinctive and memorable rationale that tightly links prior experience to this exact mandate.

features.name: Security assessment practice
features.description: Hands-on experience assessing systems for security issues through review, threat modeling, attack-surface analysis, or remediation validation.

levels.descriptor: No assessment experience is shown.
Shows only general security interest or vocabulary without direct assessment work.
Shows direct experience performing security reviews or assessments.
Shows direct assessment experience plus method detail, such as threat models, attacker mindset, attack-surface mapping, or remediation verification.

features.name: Security automation insight
features.description: How well the letter understands the role's core problem as scaling security work through automation and security-at-scale systems.

levels.descriptor: Frames the role generically as software or security work, with little sign of understanding the specific problem the team solves.
Mentions automation or security scale in broad terms, but without a crisp diagnosis of the underlying bottleneck.
Frames the work as reducing manual security workload or improving vulnerability handling at scale.
Articulates a precise thesis about the domain, such as scaling scarce expert judgment, treating vulnerability response as a systems problem, or multiplying one finding into fleet-wide protection.

features.name: Security credentials
features.description: Strength of formal third-party security certifications or credentials cited as evidence of security knowledge or skill.

levels.descriptor: No security certification is mentioned.
A baseline credential such as Security+ is presented.
A hands-on offensive credential such as OSCP is presented.

features.name: Security engineering philosophy
features.description: Thoughtfulness and maturity of the applicant's stated view of what security engineering is for and how it should be practiced.

levels.descriptor: Little sign of a security-specific philosophy or perspective.
Expresses seriousness about security, but only in generic terms.
Shows a clear personal lens such as attacker thinking, builder's-eye reviewing, or preference for quiet resilience.
Presents a memorable, role-relevant philosophy that convincingly shapes how the applicant builds and evaluates systems.

features.name: Vulnerability workflow automation
features.description: Direct experience building tooling that automates vulnerability intake, triage, classification, routing, deduplication, or prioritization.

levels.descriptor: No direct vulnerability-handling automation is described.
Shows general interest in automating security work, but no concrete triage example.
Gives a concrete example of building automation for vulnerability intake or report handling.
Shows clear ownership of triage automation and explains how it reduced manual work or improved flow.

other.name: Other
other.description: Captures proofreading quality and the extent to which spelling or typographical errors distract from credibility.

levels.descriptor: Contains frequent noticeable errors that repeatedly interrupt reading.
Contains several distracting errors, but remains understandable.
Contains only minor occasional errors or awkwardness.
Reads as clean, proofread, and professionally polished.
